title: The spaces of gradient and divergence-free fields are closed and the minimizers see the curl-free part
author: Jaros\l aw Mederski$^{*}$ and Andrzej Szulkin
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Lemma 2.1 of the article (source label defof, source0.tex lines 561--573), that the spaces $\cV$ and $\cW$ are closed subspaces of $\Wc=\cD^{1,p}(\curl;\R^3)$ and that the norm of an element of $\cV$ controls the norm of its curl-free part, delivered with the author's own complete 50-line proof at source0.tex lines 577--626. H2: the proof is the analytic core of the decomposition machinery of the article rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must control the $L^p$-norm of the divergence-free part through the projection onto gradient fields, use the Calderon--Zygmund-type bound for that projection together with the closedness of the space of gradients, and then deduce both the closedness of $\cV$ and $\cW$ and the inequality $|u|_p\leq C|\curl u|_p$ for the elements of $\cV$; the argument is carried out for $1<p<\infty$ and requires the sharp constants used later in the paper. Reproducing that projection argument for the Sobolev-curl setting is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
